title: How Many Times?
description:
Given an array `nums` and a number `target`, return how many times `target` appears in the array.

Example: for `nums = [2, 5, 2, 7]` and `target = 2`, return `2`.
hints: Concept: a counter is a variable that starts at 0 and goes up by 1 each time something happens. `count++` adds 1 to `count`.
Approach: look at every number. When it equals `target`, add 1 to the counter. Return the counter at the end.

workedExample.title: Count the Zeros
workedExample.description: Return how many numbers in `nums` are exactly 0.
workedExample.explanation:
This is the **counting** pattern: a counter starting at 0, a loop over everything, and an `if` that decides what to count.

Only the condition inside the `if` changes from problem to problem. Note that `==` compares two values, while `=` stores a value.

walkthrough.note: nums[0] is 2, which matches the target. count becomes 1.

mistakes.hint: You stopped counting after the first match. Don't `return` inside the loop; keep counting and return after it.
You counted every number. Only add 1 when `nums[i] == target`.
